$comment: Ground truth for the testbed. Every planted defect has an entry naming the tool that
should surface it and the assertion that proves it did.
expectedFail: true means the assertion currently does NOT hold and that is a known
bug in the MCP server under test, documented in that repo's REVIEW.md. The harness
reports these separately and does not fail the run. When one starts passing, the
underlying bug has been fixed and the flag should be removed.
pendingFixture: true means the defect is not yet correctly planted in the testbed.
That is our gap, not the server's, and it is tracked separately so it is never
Assertion ops: includes, notIncludes, equals, gt, gte, lt, lte, matches, lengthGte,
isError, noError. Paths support dot access and [*] to flatten an array.

build.title: Baseline reports substantially fewer problems than regressed
build.why: False-positive control. Note the baseline still gets a 'critical' of its own: severity is keyed to absolute byte thresholds, not to the size of the app, so a small well-built app is graded like a large bloated one.

build.title: Heavy statically-imported route is flagged for code splitting
/report is the heaviest route in the regressed build
build.why: Route keys come straight from app-build-manifest.json, so App Router entries carry the internal /page suffix.

build.title: A package dominating a widely-shared chunk is identified
Two resolved copies of lodash are reported as duplicates
build.why: Never once exercised before this testbed: weather-app returned duplicateCount 0.

build.title: The react-feather barrel is flagged for optimizePackageImports
build.why: NOT PLANTED YET. trace_import finds a single 2 KB react-feather module, so the whole barrel is not actually being pulled in and there is nothing for the tool to detect. The fixture needs enough distinct icons imported across >= 2 client routes, with optimizePackageImports absent, before this assertion means anything. react-feather is used because Next's built-in optimizePackageImports list already covers the popular icon packs.

build.title: Shared baseline weight is called out
Growth between the two builds is detected and attributed
compare_builds ranks /report as a top grower
CSS growth is reported without inventing phantom chunks
build.why: Content-hashed CSS filenames differ between builds; naive matching reports the whole stylesheet as new on both sides.

build.title: Vendored react-dom is not split from the direct copy
build.why: extractPackageName takes the LAST node_modules segment, so next/dist/compiled/react-dom buckets as 'next'. See perfonext-build-mcp/REVIEW.md H2.

build.title: A package is never reported as larger than the chunk containing it
build.why: topPackages.emittedBytes is the package's share of the chunk's emitted size, so it cannot exceed emittedSizeBytes.

build.title: The synthetic /layout key is not reported as a user-facing route
build.why: app-build-manifest.json records root-layout client components under a /layout key. get_largest_routes now omits that key so layout-mounted chunks can still count as shared.

profiler.title: The efficient variant burns far less CPU than the slow one
read_source_context shows the lines that actually carry the ticks
profiler.why: Fixed in profiler-mcp v0.6.0: the window is now sized from the actual tick extent (scoped to the primary node's file) instead of a fixed +/-10 around the declaration, and a hiddenTicks/warning field reports any ticks still outside it. See perfonext-profiler-mcp/REVIEW.md H1 (resolved).

profiler.title: The quadratic scan is a top hotspot
CPU spent inside npm packages is attributed
profiler.why: Never exercised before this testbed: aqi-monitoring's profile was 100% user code, so this returned 'No npm package frames found'.

profiler.title: Optimization patterns are detected in the slow variant
A directory is rejected with a clear, actionable error
profiler.why: load_profile intentionally accepts only a single profile file path — multi-file/directory ingestion is a deferred roadmap item (auto-selecting a 'main thread' by sample count was rejected as unreliable, since CPU-bound work is often offloaded to worker_threads). A directory input is a user error, not a case to enumerate or recover from; v0.6.0 replaced the raw EISDIR message with a clear one explaining the single-file contract.

render.title: Baseline produces far fewer commits than regressed
render.why: Live captures now report the same commitCount (~18) on both apps: react-scan/lite records React commits, and the interaction script drives the same input sequence. The baseline still has fewer analyzable components because memo/useCallback keep the tree from exploding. Re-check R0-control and R1 after recapture. Headless caps requestAnimationFrame at 60Hz and can lower animation-driven work.

render.title: Live capture yields exact change descriptions
render.why: Requires a React profiling build. A plain next start silently yields commitCount 0. A headless browser does not: react-scan/lite installs the profiling hook itself.

render.title: The rerender storm is visible as extra components in the same commits
render.why: Paired with R0-control. Unstable context and unmemoized props re-render extra components inside the same React commits, so commitCount no longer separates the apps. componentCount does.

render.title: Rerender causes are attributed with exact evidence

adversarial.title: A truncated profile fails cleanly rather than crashing
A zero-sample profile does not crash the parser
adversarial.why: Fixed in profiler-mcp v0.6.0: computeTotalTime no longer uses a non-null assertion on a dangling child id (the actual crash cause — 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading selfTime)'), so a profile with no samples now loads successfully and reports sampleCount: 0.

adversarial.title: Stats written without ids/modulesSpace produce a warning, not silence
adversarial.why: This is the exact silent-failure the collection recipe exists to prevent.

adversarial.title: A manifest from another Next.js major is handled
An empty build directory produces a clear error
